The right-hand side in the above can be made arbitrarily by density of $\cV$ in $\cU_o$.

issues.failure_explanation: Kernel universality establishes density of the feature span only in the sup-norm topology of $C(\overline D)$. The claimed density in $\cU_o$ (e.g. $H^2(D)$ in the paper's examples) requires approximating derivatives in the $\cU_o$-norm, which sup-norm density does not imply; no compatibility between the $C^2$-topology of the Gaussian features and $\cU_o$ is assumed, and the needed argument (e.g. Gaussian quasi-interpolation with centers in $D_1\setminus\overline D$ approximating smooth functions in $C^2$, combined with the assumed density of smooth functions in $\cU_o$) is missing. The claim is true for the intended Sobolev choices, but as written the inference is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: However, a key advantage is that $\cV$ is dense in $\cU_o$. This property follows from the fact that the Gaussian kernel is a ``universal kernel'', meaning that finite linear combinations of its shifts can approximate any continuous function on a compact set arbitrarily well

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard approximation lemma (quasi-interpolation by the Gaussian features with centers in $D_1\setminus\overline D$, converging in $C^2$ on $\overline D$) together with a compatibility condition linking $C^2(\overline D)$ to $\cU_o$; all subsequent claims are then preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The construction of $u^\delta$ in thm:error_bound ('by density of $\cV$ in $\cU_o$'), and the motivational step preceding thm:convergence, rest on an unestablished premise.
issues.title: Density of V in U_o justified only by sup-norm kernel universality
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is standard and contained, the statement is true for the paper's intended function spaces, and no claim, rate, or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \Cref{eq:continuity}, $u_{K,\alpha}$ and all its partial derivatives up to second order converge pointwise to the corresponding derivatives of $u_{\alpha}$ as $K\to\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: Pointwise convergence does not imply equicontinuity, so the stated justification for invoking Arzelà–Ascoli is an invalid inference. The valid route — the uniform bound on $\{\mu_{K,\alpha}\}$ in $M(\Omega)$ established earlier in the same proof, combined with the continuity of $\cN:M(\Omega)\to C^{2,\gamma}(D_1)$ from prop:neural_network_mapping, which yields equi-Lipschitz families — is never invoked. The claimed $C^1(\overline D)$ convergence is true, but a necessary step is missing as written.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the functions $u_{K,\alpha}$ and all their first-order derivatives are equicontinuous, and the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem tells us that $u_{K,\alpha}$ converges to $u_{\alpha}$ in $C^1(\overline{D})$ as $K\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing one-line argument: the uniform measure bounds give uniform $C^{2,\gamma}$-bounds on $\{u_{K,\alpha}\}$, hence equicontinuity of the functions and their first derivatives, after which Arzelà–Ascoli applies.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the $C^1$-convergence assertion in thm:convergence is incomplete; the assertion itself is recoverable with the paper's own tools.
issues.title: Equicontinuity in the proof of the convergence theorem asserted from pointwise convergence
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and routine, uses bounds already established in the same proof, and changes no claim, rate, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted uniform two-sided relative accuracy of the quadrature over $\cV$-balls is false. Counterexample within the paper's own framework (e.g. $-\Delta u=0$ with zero Dirichlet data): for any collocation configuration with minimum spacing $h$ and any $M>0$, the single feature $v=c\,\varphi(\cdot;y,\sigma)$ has $\|v\|_\cV\le|c|\le M$, and its residual $\cE[v]=-\Delta v$ is a bump of width $\sigma$ and height $\sim|c|\sigma^{s-d-2}$. Choosing $y$ between collocation points and $\sigma\ll h$ makes every sampled residual exponentially small, so $\hat L(v)\approx0$ while $L(v)\sim c^2\sigma^{2(s-d-2)+1}>0$, violating $L(v)\le2\hat L(v)$; placing $y$ at a collocation point violates $\hat L(v)\le2L(v)$ by a factor $\sim h/\sigma$. The root cause is that $\cV$-bounded sets contain arbitrarily narrow features, so quadrature has uniform absolute but not relative accuracy; the constants $C(K,\|e\|_{C^{0,\gamma}})$ in (eq:generalization) do not exist, and the small-loss regime where thm:error_bound applies the lemma is exactly where it fails.

failure_location.quote:
Given $M>0$, there exists $K = K(M) \in \N$, such that for any $v\in \cV$ with $\| v\|_{\cV} \leq M$
\[
\frac{1}{2} \hat{L}(v) \leq  L(v) \leq 2 \hat{L}(v)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma by an additive-error version, e.g. $L(v)\le C\hat L(v)+C(M)K^{-\beta}$ for quasi-uniform collocation designs (provable by splitting the representing measure into coarse $\sigma\gtrsim h$ and fine $\sigma\ll h$ parts and using the uniform Hölder bounds), and choose $K(\delta)$ accordingly in thm:error_bound.
issues.overall_effect: thm:error_bound's proof is invalid (the lemma is applied both to $u^\delta$ and to the minimizer $u_{K,\alpha}$), so the finite-$K$ error-bound guarantee — one of the paper's headline 'provable convergence guarantees' — is unproven as stated.
issues.title: Generalization lemma (two-sided equivalence of continuous and empirical losses) is false
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma is false and a headline theorem's proof collapses, but a comparable error bound survives under a repair requiring a new contained lemma and a mild quasi-uniformity assumption on the collocation design; no global restructuring or major loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Exact solution is obtained using finite difference method with transformation $u = -\epsilon \log v$ (same as~\cite{chen2021solving})
The unique viscosity solution in this case is $u_{\text{visc}} = \dist(x, \partial D) = \min(1 - |x_1|, 1 -|x_2|)$.
We then check the convergence towards the unique viscosity solution as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$.

issues.failure_explanation:
Two inconsistencies in the specification. (i) The residual drops the square on $|
abla u|$ relative to the displayed equation $|
abla u|^2+\epsilon\Delta u=f^2$, so the method as defined solves $|
abla u|+\epsilon\Delta u=f^2$, a different PDE. (ii) The sign of the viscosity term is anti-diffusive: for either the displayed equation or the residual as written (with $f\equiv1$), any classical solution satisfies $u\le0$ in $D$ (at an interior positive maximum, $
abla u=0$ and $\Delta u\le0$ force $1=|
abla u|^2+\epsilon\Delta u\le0$ or $1=|
abla u|+\epsilon\Delta u\le0$), and in the analogous 1D problem the solutions converge to $-\dist(x,\partial D)$, not to the claimed viscosity solution $u_{	ext{visc}}=\dist(x,\partial D)\ge0$. Moreover, the transformation $u=-\epsilon\log v$ used for the reference solution linearizes only the standard equation $|
abla u|^2-\epsilon\Delta u=f^2$ (reducing it to $\epsilon^2\Delta v=f^2v$), so the reference 'exact solution' corresponds to yet another equation than the one displayed. The section's setup and its convergence-to-viscosity-solution claim are therefore false/inconsistent as written.

failure_location.quote: In this case, $\cE[u] = |\nabla u| + \epsilon \upDelta u - f^{2}$ and $\cB[u] = u$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the equation and residual to $|\nabla u|^2-\epsilon\Delta u=f^2$, i.e. $\cE[u]=|\nabla u|^2-\epsilon\Delta u-f^2$, consistent with the log-transform reference solution and the viscosity limit; the remainder of the section then becomes consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The Eikonal experiment's stated mathematical basis is internally inconsistent; its central conclusion (convergence to the unique viscosity solution $\dist$) is false for the equation as specified, and the reported results cannot be reproduced from the stated residual.
issues.title: Regularized Eikonal equation and residual mis-specified (missing square; wrong viscosity sign)
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and preserves the experiment's conclusions, but as written the section defines and solves a different (anti-diffusive) PDE than claimed and its headline convergence claim is mathematically false; the consistent correction must be inferred by reconciling three mutually inconsistent specifications (displayed PDE, residual, transformation/viscosity claims), which exceeds a routine typo fix though it causes no global loss.
